evidence.quote: STRING links IL12B and IL23R with combined score 0.99 (experimental 0.93, database 0.65, text-mining 0.46).

excluded.reason: a STRING edge (experimental 0.00, database 0.80, text-mining 0.90) names both proteins but cannot carry 'activates'
'Interleukin-23 signaling' over-represented in the run's gene set (3 of 11 entities); says nothing of IL23R activating TYK2

statements.text: TYK2 raises the amount of T-helper 17 cells
statements.note: the run's object is the cell type 'T-helper 17 cell' with polarity positive; the mechanism reads it as 'differentiation and expansion of Th17 cells', so the effect is on the cell type's amount (OBA:0005025), a phenotype target

excluded.reason: GO 'positive regulation of T-helper 17 type immune response' enriched among the run's own genes IL12B, IL23R, TYK2 (3 of 15); an over-representation result, not TYK2 driving Th17 cells

statements.text: the amount of T-helper 17 cells goes with psoriasis (direction not stated)
statements.sign_note: the run's polarity is unknown and no cited text names Th17 cells, so the direction is none

excluded.reason: GWAS row for the TYK2 missense allele rs34536443-G and psoriasis (OR 1.88); names no Th17 cells
says only that ustekinumab targets IL12B and reached approval; names neither Th17 cells nor psoriasis
says only that deucravacitinib targets TYK2 and reached approval; names neither Th17 cells nor psoriasis

statements.text: TRAF3IP2 raises the risk of psoriasis

excluded.reason: GWAS row: missense allele rs33980500-T (author-reported gene TRAF3IP2) goes with psoriasis, OR 1.52; an allele association, and the row does not say how the allele changes TRAF3IP2
an Open Targets association score (0.67) carries no sign
says only that iguratimod targets TRAF3IP2 and reached approval; does not name psoriasis

hyp1_il23_axis.note: one claim per gene (IL12B, IL23R, TYK2); title and mechanism say IL-23 signalling through TYK2 drives psoriasis. The chain cannot compose: step 1 is binds (no sign), and step 4 (Th17 cell amount with psoriasis) is an unsigned association, so the signed steps 2 and 3 (IL23R to TYK2 activity, TYK2 to Th17 cell amount) reach no disease

hyp2_traf3ip2_il17.note: a one-step chain, gene to disease; the IL-17 receptor signalling in the title has no step

findings.detail: the chain opens with an unsigned 'binds' step and closes with an 'associated_with' step of unknown polarity, so no claim of the hypothesis can reach psoriasis with a sign even if every citation held
'IL23R activates TYK2' cites a STRING edge with no experimental channel (0.00) and a Reactome over-representation result; neither states activation
two of the H1 citations are enrichment results computed on the run's own chosen genes (IL12B, IL23R, TYK2): they show the genes share annotations, not that one step causes the next

'T-helper 17 cell associated with psoriasis' cites a TYK2-locus GWAS row and two drug-approval records (ustekinumab/IL12B, deucravacitinib/TYK2); none names Th17 cells, and the drug records do not name psoriasis
'TRAF3IP2 leads to psoriasis (+)' cites an allele association, an unsigned Open Targets score and an iguratimod approval that does not name psoriasis; nothing states a direction for TRAF3IP2 itself

both GWAS rows name a missense risk allele (rs33980500-T, rs34536443-G with risk-allele frequency 0.953) but neither says whether the allele raises or lowers the protein's function, so the gene-level '+' of H2 (and of TYK2 in H1) does not follow from them

the node 'T-helper 17 cell' is a cell type used as an effect object with no quantity: the step note reads it as 'Th17 immune responses', the mechanism as 'differentiation and expansion of Th17 cells'; curated as the cell amount (OBA:0005025), the reading 'expansion' gives
the title and mechanism are about TRAF3IP2 as the IL-17 receptor adaptor in skin cells, but the chain is one step, TRAF3IP2 to psoriasis, so none of that mechanism is stated or checkable

the mechanism says it is 'strongly supported by genetic associations and the clinical efficacy of targeted therapies like Ustekinumab and Deucravacitinib', yet the cited ChEMBL rows give only target and approval stage (no indication, no efficacy) and the run itself rates confidence 'low' and support 'speculative'

the corpus definition of GO:0072538 'T-helper 17 type immune response' says the response 'is associated with pathological autoimmune conditions such as multiple sclerosis, arthritis and psoriasis', closer to the step than anything the run cited (not attached: it is a process, not the cell type, and the run did not cite it)
neither hypothesis lists supporting or contradicting evidence; every source is a chain citation, so there were no contradicting citations to judge

the guide has no row for an effect on a cell type: render.py limits an amount target to chemical, protein or gene, and the grounding table lists HP/MP/PATO for phenotypes but not OBA, though render.py maps OBA to phenotype and OBA:0005025 'T-helper 17 cell amount' expresses the step as a phenotype target
the run's abstention (EGFL8, GLE1, UHRF2: 'no shared mechanism') is a claim with its own evidence, and curated.json has no place to judge it

sources.py fetches only hypothesis citations, so the abstention's evidence (Q99944, Q53GS7, Q96PU4, rs3117182, reactome:coverage) is not in sources.json and its claim that EGFL8 has a genome-wide psoriasis association (rs3117182) cannot be checked

the guide's claim subject is the chain's first node, but when the first step is 'binds' (a rel) that subject can never have a route, so the IL12B claim is no-route by construction rather than for want of evidence

'IL23R activates TYK2' skips IL12RB1: the corpus UniProt records of the run's own genes put TYK2 on 'a TYK2-associated receptor chain (IFNAR1, IL12RB1, IL10RB or IL13RA1)' (P29597) and say IL23R 'Interacts with JAK2' (Q5VWK5), and the cited STRING edge has experimental score 0.00

the run had a UniProt specialist but cited no UniProt text; TRAF3IP2's record (O43734) states the title's mechanism ('Essential adapter molecule in IL17A-mediated signaling'), which no chain step or citation carries

audit.before: unexpressed, other_construct: 'needs an amount or differentiation target on a cell type'
audit.after: statement S5: TYK2 effect pos, target phenotype th17CellAmount (OBA:0005025 'T-helper 17 cell amount'); STRING:GO:2000318 still excluded as enrichment
audit.reason: BioLean has the form: OBA:0005025 is in the corpus and render.py maps OBA to phenotype, a valid effect target (other runs use OBA and UPHENO cell-number terms this way). 'leads_to (+) T-helper 17 cell' reads as more Th17 cells, and the mechanism says 'differentiation and expansion of Th17 cells'

audit.after: th17CellAmount = OBA:0005025 (phenotype), object of S5 and subject of S3
audit.reason: steps 3 and 4 use the same run label 'T-helper 17 cell' and the run chains them through it, so they are one node; grounding step 3 as the amount and step 4 as the cell type would break a link the run made. S3 stays an unsigned assoc, so composition is unchanged (no route)

audit.before: 'step 3 has a cell type as object (unexpressed)'
audit.after: steps 2 and 3 are signed effects; the chain breaks at the binds step and the unsigned step 4
audit.reason: follows the S5 change; the reason for no route is now only the unsigned ends

audit.after: category ambiguous_label, naming the amount reading taken
audit.reason: the label was grounded (to CL:0000899, now OBA:0005025); the problem is that the run's note and mechanism give two readings

audit.item: finding biolean no_form_for (effect on a cell type)

audit.reason: the form exists; what is missing is a guide rule pointing to it. The mechanism's 'expansion' is the amount reading
the abstention covers EGFL8, GLE1 and UHRF2, not hyp1_il23_axis; the finding was attached to the wrong hypothesis
